title: Mohd. Irshad vs United India Insurance Company Limited on 10 April, 2014
doc:
Mohd. Irshad vs United India Insurance Company Limited on 10 April, 2014

 STATE CONSUMER DISPUTES REDRESSAL COMMISSION UTTARAKHAND
                         DEHRADUN

                    FIRST APPEAL NO. 139 / 2012

Mohd. Irshad S/o Sh. Hazi H. Ullah
R/o Azadnagar, Line No. 11
Haldwani, Nainital
                                            ......Appellant / Complainant

                                 Versus

United India Insurance Company Limited
through Divisional Manager
Divisional Office, Aishbagh, Kaladungi Road
Haldwani, District Nainital
                                        ......Respondent / Opposite Party

Sh. R.K. Garg, Learned Counsel for the Appellant
Sh. J.K. Jain, Learned Counsel for Respondent

Coram: Hon'ble Mr. Justice B.C. Kandpal, President
       Mr. C.C. Pant,                    Member

Dated: 10/04/2014

                               ORDER

(Per: Justice B.C. Kandpal, President):

This appeal, under Section 15 of the Consumer Protection Act, 1986, is directed by the complainant against the order dated 24.08.2012 passed by the District Forum, Nainital in consumer complaint No. 115 of 2010, whereby the District Forum has dismissed the consumer complaint filed by the complainant.

2. Briefly stated, the facts of the case as mentioned in the consumer complaint, are that the complainant - Mohd. Irshad was the registered owner of Tata Indica car No. UA04-D-8686. The said vehicle was insured with the opposite party - United India Insurance Company Limited for the period from 15.01.2010 to 14.01.2011. On 21.01.2010, the insured vehicle met with an accident at Pangoot -

2

Kilbary Road, Nainital and got damaged to the extent of 75%. The complainant lodged the claim with the insurance company and completed all the formalities. The insurance company, however, vide their letter dated 07.07.2010 repudiated the claim of the complainant as "No Claim". Alleging deficiency in service on the part of the insurance company, the complainant filed a consumer complaint before the District Forum, Nainital.

3. The insurance company filed written statement before the District Forum and pleaded that the surveyor has assessed the loss to the tune of Rs. 1,04,500/- on cash loss basis; that Sh. Chandrapal Singh Tomar was appointed as investigator, who in his investigation report stated that the complainant had sold the subject vehicle to Mohd. Irfan S/o late Mohd. Shamim on 14.05.2008 for Rs. 2,07,600/-; that a sale agreement dated 14.05.2008 was executed by the complainant in favour of Mohd. Irfan; that Mohd. Irfan had also sold the vehicle to one Smt. Kiran Bisht in October, 2009; that the loan installments of the vehicle were also paid by Mohd. Irfan; that the complainant has not given any intimation to the insurance company regarding transfer of the insured vehicle by him and, as such, the claim was not maintainable and was rightly repudiated and that there is no deficiency in service on their part.

4. The District Forum, on an appreciation of the material on record, dismissed the consumer complaint vide impugned order dated 24.08.2012. Aggrieved by the said order, the complainant has filed this appeal.

5. We have heard the learned counsel for the parties and have also perused the record.

3

6. That the sale agreement dated 14.05.2008 executed by the complainant in favour of Mohd. Irfan S/o late Mohd. Shamim, R/o Mohalla Bhawaniganj, Ramnagar, District Nainital, is on record (Paper No. 17/6 of the original record). In the said agreement, it has clearly been mentioned that the complainant has sold the subject vehicle to Mohd. Irfan for sum of Rs. 2,07,600/-. In the said agreement, it has also been mentioned that the vehicle has been handed over to the purchaser (Mohd. Irfan), which he has accepted. There is no dispute with regard to the fact that the complainant has not given any intimation to the insurer regarding sale of the insured vehicle by him. The vehicle was insured for the period from 15.01.2010 to 14.01.2011 in the name of the complainant, whereas the fact is that the vehicle was sold much prior to the said date by the complainant to Mohd. Irfan. It has also come on record that Mohd. Irfan, has, in turn, sold the vehicle to Smt. Kiran Bisht in October, 2009, much before the date of commencement of the insurance policy in question, but the insurer has also not been given any intimation with regard to this transfer of the vehicle. The complainant has also given a statement to the investigator on 17.03.2010 (Paper No. 17/7), stating therein that he has sold the subject vehicle about 1½ years back to Mohd. Irfan. In the said statement, the complainant has also stated that he has not submitted any claim form with the insurer and he has no knowledge with regard to the accident of the insured vehicle. The FIR of the accident was lodged by Sh. Rajendra Singh Bisht, the husband of Smt. Kiran Bisht, as would be evident from the copy of the FIR on record (Paper No. 5/2). Thus, it is clear that on the date of the accident, the vehicle was under the ownership and control of Smt. Kiran Bisht and the complainant was not having any insurable interest in the vehicle and he has committed breach of the terms and conditions of the contract of insurance by not giving any intimation to the insurer with regard to the sale of the vehicle by him and also by 4 getting the vehicle insured in his name inspite of the fact that the vehicle was not under his ownership and possession and he had sold the vehicle much before the date of the commencement of the policy of insurance.

7. It is a settled law that w.e.f. the date of sale of the vehicle, the insured ceases to have any insurable interest in the vehicle. It is also evident from the record that even after the sale of the vehicle, the insurance policy was fraudulently got obtained by the complainant in his favour, as on the date of the insurance, he had no insurable interest in the vehicle. The District Forum has considered all the facts and circumstances of the case and has passed a reasoned order, which does not require any interference.

8. The Hon'ble National Commission in the case of New India Assurance Company Limited Vs. Shaik Dawood; II (2013) CPJ 401 (NC), has held that the respondent did not have any insurance interest in the vehicle on the date it met with an accident and that the claim was rightly repudiated by the insurer. In the said case, the respondent did not intimate the insurance company about transfer of ownership of vehicle within 14 days of registration in his name to enable the insurance company to make necessary changes in its record and to issue a fresh certificate of insurance.

9. Learned counsel for the appellant - complainant cited a decision dated 13.03.2014 of this Commission rendered in First Appeal No. 111 of 2012; HDFC ERGO General Insurance Company Limited Vs. Sh. Balraj Singh, wherein it was held that the registered owner of the vehicle shall be deemed to be the owner of the vehicle. In the present case, as is stated above, the investigator has clearly stated in his investigation report that the complainant has sold 5 the subject vehicle to Mohd. Irfan on 14.05.2008 and he has also given a statement to this effect to the investigator. The FIR of the accident was lodged Sh. Rajendra Singh Bisht, the husband of Smt. Kiran Bisht and on the date of the accident, the vehicle was not under the ownership and control of the complainant. Learned counsel for the appellant - complainant cited another decision dated 30.10.2013 of this Commission rendered in First Appeal No. 135 of 2009; National Insurance Company Limited Vs. Sh. Mahabir Singh Bisht and another. We are unable to understand as to why this decision has been cited, as it is against the complainant's case. In the said case, the vehicle was registered in the name of Sh. Ramesh Chand Gaur and was also insured in his name. The vehicle was sold by Sh. Ramesh Chand Gaur to Sh. Mahabir Singh Bisht. In the said decision, it was held that Sh. Ramesh Chand Gaur, the registered owner of the vehicle, may file a consumer complaint. It is true that the vehicle in question is still registered in the name of the complainant, but in view of the fact that he has sold the vehicle and has also admitted this fact in his statement given to the investigator, he cease to have any insurable interest in the vehicle and the claim lodged by the complainant was rightly repudiated by the insurance company and no deficiency in service was made by the insurance company.

10. The Hon'ble National Commission in a latest judgment given in the case of Sandeep Gupta Vs. United India Insurance Company Limited and another; I (2014) CPJ 493 (NC), has held that in case the policy is not transferred in the name of transferee, the insurance company can not be held liable to pay claim in case of own damage of vehicle. In the said case, the vehicle had already been sold by Sh. Jit Singh and Sh. Prem Singh to Sh. Sandeep Gupta and it was held that they were also not entitled to any insurance claim. While coming to 6 the said conclusion, the Hon'ble National Commission has placed reliance on the decision of the Hon'ble Apex Court rendered in the case of Complete Insulations (P) Ltd. Vs. New India Assurance Company Limited; I (1996) CPJ 1 (SC) = I (1996) CLT 22 (SC) = II (1996) ACC 536 (SC). Therefore, in view of the aforesaid judgments cited above, the appeal lacks merit and is liable to be dismissed.

11. For the reasons aforesaid, the appeal is dismissed. No order as to costs. 

             (C.C. PANT)              (JUSTICE B.C. KANDPAL)
K
